raw.instructions:
You are identifying axes in a cropped line chart before calibration.
Multiple plot panels or small multiples are supported. Treat each visible panel as part of the same chart run.
Distinguish panels using clear location language such as top-left panel, right panel, lower panel, or panel title.
When naming axes or series in a multi-panel chart, include enough panel context in axis_id, location_description, series_name, or visual_description to avoid ambiguity.

Identify every visible x-axis and y-axis in every panel, including secondary axes on the top, bottom, left, or right.
For each axis, provide a stable axis_id, direction, name, unit, quantity being measured, and a brief location description.
In multi-panel charts include panel location or panel title in location_description.
If multiple axes measure the same quantity in different units, mark exactly one metric axis closest to the chart body as is_primary_for_digitization=true.
Mark other duplicate axes as is_primary_for_digitization=false and explain the ignore_reason.
If multiple axes measure different quantities, mark all of them as is_primary_for_digitization=true because different curves may use them.
Prefer metric units over imperial or US customary units. If more than one metric axis measures the same quantity, choose the one closest to the chart body.
Do not return calibration points in this step.
Identify unsupported conditions: non-line chart content, logarithmic axes, categorical axes, broken axes, unreadable labels, or charts where the line data cannot be visually traced.
If such a condition is present, return warnings and set unsupported flags where the schema allows it.
